arguments.text: If `config.Output` is nil, the log line is written to the Echo instance's logger output: `c.Logger().Output()` (middleware/logger.go, end of the returned handler). `c.Logger()` returns the per-request logger if set via `c.SetLogger(...)`, otherwise `e.Logger` — which `echo.New()` initializes to `log.New("echo")` (gommon log), whose output defaults to `os.Stdout`. That matches the field's doc comment "Optional. Default value os.Stdout." Note the nil check happens at write time, so `config.colorer.SetOutput(config.Output)` is set up with nil, but the actual write goes to the Echo logger's writer.

arguments.text: Fixed in middleware/proxy.go. Root cause: with an empty target list, `randomBalancer.Next` called `rand.Intn(0)` ("invalid argument to Intn" panic) and `roundRobinBalancer.Next` indexed `targets[0]` (index out of range). Both `Next` implementations now return nil when there are no targets, and `ProxyWithConfig` returns `echo.ErrServiceUnavailable` (503) when the balancer yields no target instead of dereferencing nil. Verified: `NewRandomBalancer(nil).Next`/`NewRoundRobinBalancer(nil).Next` return nil, the middleware responds 503 without panicking (also after removing all targets at runtime), and the full test suite passes, including `go test -race ./middleware/`.

arguments.text: It returns `echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusInternalServerError, i.(error).Error())` — i.e. a 500 "Internal Server Error" HTTPError whose message is the string form of the pooled value, obtained by asserting the value to `error` (middleware/decompress.go, in the `case GZIPEncoding:` branch of `DecompressWithConfig`). The pool's `New` function only ever returns a `*gzip.Reader` or an `error`, so the non-`*gzip.Reader` case is the error case; note that if the pooled value were neither, the `i.(error)` assertion itself would panic rather than return the HTTPError.

instructions:
. You are working in the Go repository checked out at /echo (module github.com/labstack/echo/v4, an older echo v4.2.x snapshot). There is a known bug in /echo/router.go (the radix-tree router, functions Router.Add / Router.insert / Router.Find / backtrackToNextNodeKind) whose symptom is described by the (not present in the repo) test name `TestRouterNoRoutablePath` in the root package. Your job is to FIND the concrete reproduction, i.e. a minimal sequence of `e.router.Add(method, path, handler)` calls plus a request path passed to `e.router.Find(method, path, ctx)` (or an `e.ServeHTTP` request) that makes the router PANIC (index out of range, nil pointer dereference, etc.) or hang in an infinite loop, or return a clearly wrong result (e.g. a handler that does not match the request path, or a non-NotFound handler for a path that matches no route).

Method: write a temporary Go test file `/echo/zz_fuzz_router_test.go` (package echo) that brute-force searches route-set/path combinations. Suggested approach: build random route sets from a small alphabet of path segments (static segments like "a", "b", "c", params like ":id", wildcards like "*"), e.g. paths drawn from a list like ["/", "/a", "/a/b", "/a/:id", "/a/*", "/:id", "/:id/b", "/:id/*", "/a/:id/c", "/*", "/a/b/*", "/a/*/c", "/:a/:b", "/:a/*"], register them all as GET routes on a fresh `e := New()` (use `e.router` and `e.router.Add`), then call `r.Find(http.MethodGet, somePath, c)` for request paths drawn from a similar list plus odd ones ("", "/", "//", "/a/", "/a/b/", "/a/b/c", "/x", "/x/y", "/a/x", "/a/b/c/d", paths with trailing/leading slashes, paths with ':' or '*' characters in them). Wrap each Find+handler invocation in a func with `defer recover()` so a panic is caught, and run each Find in a goroutine with a `select` on a time.After(2*time.Second) to detect infinite loops (abandon the goroutine after timeout). Iterate over many combinations (e.g. all subsets of size 1..4 of the route list, or a seeded random search with thousands of iterations) and print the FIRST minimal failing case: the exact route paths added, the request path, and the panic message / hang / wrong handler. Also verify the expected behaviour yourself: for a request path that matches no registered route, `ctx.Handler()` must be NotFoundHandler (404), and for a path that matches a route it must be that route's handler with correct params.

IMPORTANT: do NOT modify any existing file except creating/deleting your own temporary test file `zz_fuzz_router_test.go` (delete it when done, or leave it but it must not break `go test ./...` — deleting it is preferred). Do not touch router.go or any other source file; only report findings. Do not use the internet.

Report back: (1) the minimal reproduction (exact route registrations + request path + observed wrong behaviour), (2) the exact line(s) in router.go responsible and your analysis of why, (3) whether the failure is a panic, a hang, or a wrong-handler result, (4) any other router bugs you found with reproductions. If you find nothing after a thorough search, say so explicitly and list what you tried.
